source.title: Rethinking Semantic Collaborative Integration: Why Alignment Is Not Enough
source.authors: Maolin Wang; Dongze Wu; Jianing Zhou; Hongyu Chen; Beining Bao; Yu Jiang; Chenbin Zhang; Chang Wang; Jian Liu; Lei Sha

record.file_problem: The paper text is substantially present. Some figure text and table layout are garbled or flattened, making certain table cells difficult to assign reliably.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results challenging global low-capacity alignment as a general integration principle: mappings fit training items but transfer poorly to unseen items, and semantic and collaborative recommendation outputs show complementarity.
record.gate_note: The directly relevant experiment freezes the encoders and probes mappings from semantic to collaborative representations. Top-20 recommendation-overlap results are also recorded, but as a related output-agreement finding rather than a direct measurement of representation geometry. Ranking-performance comparisons of fusion methods are omitted because they do not measure alignment itself. Some alignment-probe table values are not assigned to individual models because the extracted table layout is ambiguous.
record.test_reason: The study freezes two independently trained item encoders: BGE-M3 text embeddings with a learned 64-d projection, and LightGCN collaborative embeddings. It fits linear and MLP maps from the semantic space to the collaborative space and scores them on training and unseen items with R2, cosine, neighbourhood overlap and Recall. These results bear directly on whether one model's representations map onto another's with little loss (V4), on whether measured alignment depends on the metric and the items used (V6), and on whether alignment is incomplete (V7). The paper argues that low-capacity global alignment is wrong as a default, so this is T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that semantic and collaborative representations are partially shared, heterogeneous views and that low-capacity global maps underfit while high-capacity maps overfit, so neither recovers collaborative geometry on unseen items. The record omits that they also report a minimal norm-concat-norm fusion beating alignment-based recommenders, and that they advocate complementarity-aware fusion over alignment as the default.
record.recipe_differences: The study probes mappings between frozen semantic and collaborative recommender embeddings, rather than testing the original cross-model convergence claim across scale. It also evaluates recommendation-list complementarity. The paper describes its approach as a perspective with empirical analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Mapping capacity and whether items are in the training or unseen test split affect the reported alignment-probe outcome. The paper evaluates several metrics, but the extracted table layout makes some model-by-metric values ambiguous.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-20 recommendation lists and correct-hit sets from the semantic and collaborative baselines overlap little (List Jaccard 6–19%). Complementarity ratios exceed 55% on Movies, Books and Games, even though the two baselines perform comparably.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained content-based and interaction-based recommenders make largely different correct predictions at the output level. This is output complementarity, not representation convergence.

record.problems: The paper studies recommendation encoders and does not test model scale or capability. The central mapping probe is one-way and uses one recommendation setting. The reported test-item outcomes are mainly qualitative in the text, and extracted table formatting prevents reliable assignment of all model-specific metric values. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the relevant results.
record.rows_left_out: The alignment-probe tables report additional model-by-metric cells, but several columns and model labels are flattened or interleaved in the extracted text, so those values were not assigned to individual subjects. Section 3.4 and Tables 6–9 report recommendation performance and fusion results; omitted because those results do not directly measure representation alignment. Figure 2 contains further complementarity plots, but the detailed figure-only values were not extracted.

untested.parts: All of V1. There is no model-size or capability sweep; there is one pair of encoders.
All of V2. There are no vision-language paired image–caption comparisons.
All of V3. There is no same-architecture, different-seed comparison.

The following are untested: the reverse direction (collaborative to semantic); stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping; and other model families or modalities beyond one text encoder and one graph recommender.
All of V5. No neurons, SAE features or circuits are compared.
The following are untested: varying neighbour count k for the neighbourhood metrics, out-of-distribution datasets beyond the item split, and the probe on datasets other than the one reported.
Whether alignment plateaus with model capability, and whether shared data or objectives (rather than a common model of reality) explain the alignment, are untested.

missing.what: Linear-map results on unseen items: R2 0.166, Cos 0.415, GeoJac 0.044, RankCor 0.322, ListJac 0.039, Recall(Ps) 0.0251 vs Recall(CF) 0.1005. MLP-0: R2 0.161, Recall(Ps) 0.0473. These are the main V4 test of a simple map on held-out items.
Metric disagreement on unseen items. For MLP-2, ListJac is 0.504 while GeoJac is 0.025, RankCor 0.166 and R2 -0.487. MLP-3 is similar (ListJac 0.485, R2 -0.495).

The full training-item capacity sweep. Identity: R2 -0.076, ListJac 0.001, Recall(Ps) 0.0012. MLP-0: R2 0.308. MLP-1: R2 0.475, ListJac 0.178. Recall(CF) is 0.1095 throughout. The table is reconstructable despite the flattened layout.
Qualitative t-SNE evidence that the collaborative space has a popularity core while the semantic space is organised by content. There is no number.

record.verdict_notes: The setting is recommendation: one text encoder (BGE-M3 with a learned 64-d projection trained with InfoNCE on interaction histories) against LightGCN, on Amazon data. The probe's results section does not state which dataset it uses. The semantic projection was trained on the same interaction data as LightGCN, so the two spaces are not fully independent; this weakens any causal reading for V7. The probe is one-way only, with no uncertainty estimates. The reader's V7 'challenges' labels were reversed: incomplete alignment supports V7, which is itself a challenge version. Contrary to the record, the Table 4 and 5 cells can be assigned: the Table 5 rows are clean, and Table 4 matches the text's linear values (R2 0.171, ListJac 0.039).

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, and no comparison of independently trained models across architectures, objectives, data, or modalities as a function of scale.
No vision-language model comparison on paired images and captions, or scale/performance trend across such models.
No same-architecture, different-initialization or seed comparison.

Tests mappings from semantic item representations to collaborative representations in one recommender setting; does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or other model families.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

Uses multiple alignment and retrieval metrics and compares training with unseen test items, but does not systematically vary metric settings such as neighbour count or evaluate out-of-distribution datasets.
Tests incomplete transfer between semantic and collaborative views, but does not establish that shared training data or objectives cause alignment, or test a common-reality explanation.

relationships.condition: Low-capacity (linear) semantic→collaborative map on training items
relationships.reason: On training items the linear map explains about 17% of the target variance (R2 0.171, r1). Neighbour-list overlap is near zero (ListJac 0.039 vs 0.001 for Identity, r2). Recall(Ps) is 0.0288 against a ceiling of 0.1095. Unseen-item values are similar (Table 5, not in rows; see missing).
relationships.display_finding: The linear map explained about 17% of training-item variance (R²=0.171), achieved neighbour-list overlap of 0.039 versus 0.001 for Identity, and Recall(Ps) of 0.0288 versus a 0.1095 ceiling; unseen-item results were similar.
